title: What is known about 1RB0LD_0LC0RE_1LA0RD_0RB0LD_1RC1RF_1RA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_0LC0RE_1LA0RD_0RB0LD_1RC1RF_1RA---.
intro: This six-state machine is a holdout of the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. In its first regime the machine is exactly two counters fed by one engine: per pair of visits the left side gets 3 (binary) and the right side gets 1 (base 3); these event rules are proved in Lean for every size (kernel), and a simulator built on them reproduces the run step for step through the first regime (computed, py/phase1.py). Each overflow of the left counter changes the layout and writes junk into the base-3 side; halting needs one of the sweeps after an overflow to find three 1s, which has not happened in 2·1011 steps (24 close calls).

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The sweeps of the run
claims.text: The shift rules the machine uses in its run (every sweep met when the symbolic simulator runs from many configurations of the run), each for every number of copies.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 179 cells have been visited and 70 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: E1 is rare and always followed by a 0
claims.text: E1, the only way into F, is used 24 times in the first 2·10<sup>11</sup> steps, each time followed by F reading a 0; apart from the first five (before step 152,485), each within about 600 steps after a left-end visit, in the sweep to the right that follows it, at cells 44 to 127.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: The only halting transition is F on 1, and F is entered only from E on 1 (1RF), and E (on 1) from B on 1 (0RE): a configuration halts two steps later if and only if it is B> 1 1 1 (halt_iff_2, proved by a case split on the cells the head reads), so a halting run from blank passes through it (halts_blank_pred_2).

claims.title: Base 2 on the left, base 3 on the right
claims.text: Between the left-end visits at steps 304,258,861 and 549,553,736 the turns of the head per cell halve every 4 cells on the left and fall by a factor of 3.0 every 3 cells on the right; the turns of the busiest cell between consecutive right-end extensions grow by factors of 3 (597,879, 1,793,606, 5,380,848).

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/exp
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.056). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.074).

claims.title: One count, two bases
claims.text: Read off the run: each visit to the engine adds 1 to a binary counter on the left and to a base-3 counter (digits 01, 11, 10) on the right.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts only if B meets 1 1 1; it has come close (E1) 13 times in 109 steps.

claims.title: The event rules of the first regime, for all sizes
claims.text: At an event (A on cell 65) with tape 1 H 0110 low | phase R 01: a 111-event adds 1 to the binary counter low (digits 1000/1010) in 12n+12 steps for n carried ones; a 110-event adds 2 to low and 1 to the base-3 counter R (digits 001/011/010) in 12k+12n+40, +44 or +52 steps; when low wraps, H (digits 0100/0101) gets 3, in all four cases of H mod 4 and every number j of carried ones. 35 theorems, each for all n, k, j.

claims.title: The two counters reproduce the run
claims.text: A simulator that applies only these rules (with their proved step counts), started from the tape at step 9,021,183, agrees with the direct run cell for cell and step for step at all 466,024 events up to step 31,040,523, where H overflows.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2·10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: A direct run of 2·10<sup>11</sup> steps without a halt.

claims.title: Left-end visits are a clockwork, the layout shifts at each
claims.text: The left end is visited when H overflows; from event 1,877,435 on, the periods last 1,398,096, 1,398,096, 2,796,200, 2,796,200, 5,592,404, 5,592,404, 11,184,810, 11,184,810 and 44,739,242 events (about 4/3·2<sup>k</sup>). Each visit moves the boundary between H and low one 2-cell symbol right and writes digits 110/101/100 into the start of R; low is used up at step 9,327,411,783, and after the visit at step 106,434,757,217 the engine itself moves (no A on cell 65 up to 2·10<sup>11</sup>; at step 1.065·10<sup>11</sup> the head works near cell 140).

claims.title: The engine of the new epoch
claims.text: From the tape at step 1.065·10<sup>11</sup>, 2·10<sup>9</sup> more steps stay within cells −44..192; the head is in state A on cell 138 32,383,797 times (every 61.8 steps), with events of two kinds alternating exactly, as in the first epoch, but in other words.

claims.title: Can a reset sweep find 1 1 1?
claims.text: The machine halts exactly when B meets 1 1 1. The event rules never do; the open question is what the sweeps after left-end visits find in the junk of R, in the later periods and epochs, whose rules are not yet written as one family.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine feeds two counters from one engine: per pair of visits, 3 is added to a binary number on the left and 1 to a base-3 number on the right. Each time the left one overflows the layout shifts and junk piles up on the right. It halts only if a sweep after an overflow finds three 1s in a row; 24 close calls in 2·10<sup>11</sup> steps, all misses.

facts.text: No halt in a direct run.
Event rules of the first regime, each for every size.
Reproduced step for step by the two-counter simulator.
Close calls: uses of E1, the only way into F.

sections.heading: One engine, two counters
html: Watch the head at one cell, cell 65 (counting from the start cell), in state A: call each such moment an event. From step about 107 on, the tape at an event reads, left to right,

partdigitsmeaning
H0100 = 0, 0101 = 1binary, most significant first
low1000 = 0, 1010 = 1binary, lowest digit next to the head
phase111 or 110alternates every event
R001 = 0, 011 = 1, 010 = 2base 3, lowest digit first

A 111-event adds 1 to low. A 110-event adds 2 to low and 1 to R. When low wraps around, H gets 3. So every pair of events adds 3 to the left side and 1 to the right side: after n pairs the left side holds 3n in binary and the right side holds n in base 3.
A real example from the run (steps 9,021,183 to 9,021,575): low goes 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15 and wraps to 1 while H goes from 2 to 5; R goes 3377, 3377, 3378, 3378, 3379, 3379, 3380, 3380, 3381.

These rules are theorems: lean/Events.lean proves each kind of event for every number of carried digits, with its exact step count (for example 12n+12 steps for a 111-event that carries over n ones). A simulator that uses nothing but these rules reproduces the actual run cell for cell and step for step at all 466,024 events from step 9,021,183 to step 31,040,523.

sections.heading: Every overflow shifts the layout
html: When H overflows, the carry runs to the left end of the tape, which grows by 2 cells; a sweep to the right resets H and rewrites the start of R. After each such visit the boundary between H and low sits one 2-cell symbol further right, and digits of a new kind (110, 101, 100) pile up at the start of R as junk. Inside each period the machine is again a set of counters with simple rules (for instance, in the period from step 114,227,597 to 297,999,547 a two-digit junk counter runs through 9 states in 9 events while R gains 8), but each period has its own rule.

The periods last about 4/3·2k events, each length twice: a clockwork. At step 9,327,411,783 low is used up and every event costs about 2,200 steps instead of 400; after the visit at step 106,434,757,217 the engine moves away from cell 65 altogether (at step 1.065·1011 the head works near cell 140): a new epoch, not decoded yet.

sections.heading: Twenty-four close calls
html: The machine halts only in F reading 1, and F is entered only from E1. So it halts exactly when state B meets three 1s in a row (B> 1 1 1: B1 = 0RE, E1 = 1RF, F1 halts). In 2·1011 steps E1 is used 24 times; every time F then read a 0. After step 152,484 every one of them comes in the sweep that follows a left-end visit (within about 600 steps), at cells from 44 to 127, most often in the pattern 1000 [1] 0101.

The event rules never meet 1 1 1, so the counters by themselves cannot halt the machine. The question is entirely about what the sweeps after an overflow find in the junk at the start of R. The digit 111 has appeared there once, for two events right after the visit at step 114,227,597, but no sweep reached it in state B.

sections.heading: What would settle it
html: Write the rules of all periods as one family (the boundary moves one symbol per visit, so the period number should be a parameter), decode what each reset sweep writes into R, and decode the change of epoch at step 1.064·1011. Then the close calls become a statement about the junk, and halting asks whether a sweep ever lines up with 1 1 1.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.056). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.074).
After 109 steps the tape spans 179 cells (30 left of the start, 132 right), with a density of 1s of 0.391.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Counts n twice, as 3n in binary on the left and n in base 3 on the right (proved event rules for all sizes); each left overflow shifts the layout and piles junk into the base-3 side, and it halts only if a reset sweep finds 111 (24 close calls in 2e11 steps).
